run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: Within the sampled portion of the authorized window (Prometheus ~12:58-13:00Z, Loki ~12:59:31-13:00Z, Jaeger traces 13:00:01.75-13:00:02.00Z) the hotel-reservation request path was serving normally: all 20 pods in the namespace were Running and Ready with restartCount 0, blackbox probes for frontend:5000, profile:8081, search:8082, geo:8083, rate:8084, recommendation:8085, user:8086 and reservation:8087 returned up=1, and sampled frontend spans HTTP GET /hotels and HTTP GET /recommendations returned 200 in 1.5-6.8 ms with downstream /search.Search/Nearby, /rate.Rate/GetRates, /geo.Geo/Nearby, /reservation.Reservation/CheckAvailability, /profile.Profile/GetProfiles and /recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations completing in 1-4.2 ms. The component in the namespace with observed failure evidence of its own is the cleanup-controller Deployment: pod cleanup-controller-785f8c5b5b-p26bd logs 'cleanup-controller reconciliation failed: Kubernetes API denied cleanup request with HTTP 403 Forbidden' (6 such lines counted in the last hour of the window) after logging 'ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token is Terminating; attempting controller-owned cleanup'. The cause visible in the objects is its RBAC: ClusterRole configmap-cleanup-controller, bound to ServiceAccount cleanup-controller by ClusterRoleBinding configmap-cleanup-controller, grants only get/list/watch on configmaps, while controller.py performs a PATCH on configmaps to remove finalizer cleanup.reservations.io/pending-cleanup; ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token was created and deleted at 12:59:48Z and is stuck Terminating with that finalizer. A second, unexecuted fault capability exists as a hypothesis: the mongodb-rate and mongodb-geo pod templates were replaced at 12:59:32-12:59:34Z to mount ConfigMaps failure-admin-rate/failure-admin-geo containing scripts that revoke the admin user's readWrite role on rate-db/geo-db, but admin authentication succeeded on both databases through 13:00:01Z and no revoke or authorization failure appears. History before ~12:58Z is unknown because all three telemetry stores restarted at the end of the window.

claims.text: ClusterRole configmap-cleanup-controller grants only verbs get, list and watch on resources configmaps (apiGroups ""); it grants no patch or update verb.
ClusterRoleBinding configmap-cleanup-controller binds ClusterRole configmap-cleanup-controller to ServiceAccount cleanup-controller in namespace hotel-reservation, and that ServiceAccount exists.

Deployment cleanup-controller in namespace hotel-reservation runs command ['python','/controller/controller.py'] with serviceAccountName cleanup-controller and mounts ConfigMap cleanup-controller-script at /controller.

The controller script (ConfigMap cleanup-controller-script, key controller.py) lists ConfigMaps in hotel-reservation with labelSelector app.kubernetes.io/component=reservation-cleanup and, for a ConfigMap with a deletionTimestamp and finalizer cleanup.reservations.io/pending-cleanup, issues a PATCH replacing metadata.finalizers — the only write it performs is a PATCH on configmaps.

Pod cleanup-controller-785f8c5b5b-p26bd logs 'ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token is Terminating; attempting controller-owned cleanup' followed by 'cleanup-controller reconciliation failed: Kubernetes API denied cleanup request with HTTP 403 Forbidden' repeatedly (timestamps 12:59:52-13:00:00Z), and Loki counted 6 such '403 Forbidden' lines for this pod in the last hour of the window.

ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token in namespace hotel-reservation has creationTimestamp 2026-11-21T12:59:48Z and deletionTimestamp 2026-11-21T12:59:48Z yet still exists, carrying finalizer cleanup.reservations.io/pending-cleanup and label app.kubernetes.io/component=reservation-cleanup, i.e. it is stuck Terminating because the finalizer is never removed.

All 20 pods in namespace hotel-reservation (frontend, search, rate, geo, profile, recommendation, reservation, user, the six mongodb-* pods, three memcached-* pods, consul, jaeger and cleanup-controller) were phase Running with ready true and restartCount 0 at 13:00:06Z.

Jaeger spans starting 13:00:01.75-13:00:02.00Z show frontend 'HTTP GET /hotels' with http.status_code 200 in 3538-6785 microseconds and 'HTTP GET /recommendations' with 200 in 1580-2447 microseconds, with child spans /search.Search/Nearby, /rate.Rate/GetRates, /geo.Geo/Nearby, /reservation.Reservation/CheckAvailability, /profile.Profile/GetProfiles and /recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations all completing in 1-4205 microseconds.

Prometheus blackbox probes (job blackbox-hotel-reservation) reported up=1 at 13:00:02Z for frontend.hotel-reservation:5000, profile:8081, search:8082, geo:8083, rate:8084, recommendation:8085, user:8086 and reservation:8087, and the ingress probe http://ingress-nginx-controller.ingress-nginx/api/hotels?inDate=2015-04-09&outDate=2015-04-10&lat=38.0235&lon=-122.095 also reported up=1; in the same view the targets rate.hotel-reservation:9091 and search.hotel-reservation:9092 of job hotel-reservation-application reported up=0.

mongodb-rate log shows 'Authentication succeeded' for principalName admin from remote 10.244.7.216 (the rate pod) at 12:59:40.484, 12:59:45.33x and 13:00:01.586Z, and a filtered query for revoke/grantRoles/createUser/dropUser/not authorized terms returned no revoke or authorization-failure line in the window.
mongodb-geo log shows 'Options set by command line' with security.authorization enabled and 'Authentication succeeded' for principalName admin from 10.244.7.255 at 12:59:41.2xZ.

The rate pod logged 'New session successfull', 'Generating test data', 'Successfull', 'Read profile memcashed address: memcached-rate:11211', 'Starting server' and 'Successfully registered in consul' at 12:59:40Z, and the reservation pod logged an equivalent successful startup sequence ending 'Successfully registered in consul' at 12:59:41Z.

Deployments mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate run with args ['--auth'] and mount an extra volume 'failure-script' from ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo / failure-admin-rate at /scripts, whereas the preceding ReplicaSets mongodb-geo-78487c9767 and mongodb-rate-6747cb74bf mount only the init-script volume; events show those older ReplicaSets scaled to 0 and the current ones created at 12:59:32-12:59:34Z after pods mongodb-geo-78487c9767-lsx7b and mongodb-rate-6747cb74bf-c9h75 were deleted.

ConfigMaps failure-admin-rate and failure-admin-geo contain scripts revoke-admin-rate-mongo.sh and revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh that run db.revokeRolesFromUser('admin',[{role:'readWrite',db:'rate-db'|'geo-db'}]), alongside remove-admin-mongo.sh and matching mitigate/recreate scripts.

The frontend pod's only error lines in the window are six 'grpc/lb/consul: error retrieving instances from Consul: ... dial tcp 10.96.76.105:8500: connect: connection refused' at 12:59:31Z, i.e. while the consul Service was not yet serving during pod startup; no later frontend error line was returned for the window.

The failure-admin-rate / failure-admin-geo scripts mounted into mongodb-rate and mongodb-geo at 12:59:32-12:59:34Z may be the staged fault for this environment: revoking the admin user's readWrite role on rate-db or geo-db would break the rate or geo service's database access.

Against that hypothesis at the sampled times: mongodb-rate authenticated principalName admin from the rate pod through 13:00:01.586Z and showed no revoke/grantRoles/dropUser/not authorized line, and mongodb-geo authenticated principalName admin from the geo pod at 12:59:41.2xZ; the rate service also logged a successful DB session, test-data generation and service registration.

The request path through the hotel-reservation services was not failing in the sampled traces: every sampled frontend /hotels and /recommendations span carries http.status_code 200, the deepest spans in the sample are the 6785 microsecond /hotels span and the 4205 microsecond /search.Search/Nearby span, and no span in the sampled views carries an error status or error detail.

Rejected as unsupported for the sampled window: that a hotel-reservation application service (frontend, search, rate, geo, reservation, profile, recommendation) was returning errors or timing out — its own sampled spans returned 200/success with millisecond durations and no error status was observed for those services.

gaps: Telemetry history is very short: Loki lines for namespace hotel-reservation start around 12:59:31Z, Jaeger holds traces only from 13:00:01.757Z because its pod restarted at 12:59:30Z, and a Loki query for 2026-11-20T20:00:02Z-20:05:02Z returned no data (status no_data); what happened earlier in the 24-hour authorized window is unknown.

Deployment and pod state therefore rests on the Kubernetes API reads and on the `up` blackbox view, not on kube-state-metrics series for this namespace.

Queries for kind=roles and kind=rolebindings in namespace hotel-reservation returned no objects (status no_data, e.g. c24c61c2-0452-44d7-9f74-1963aaa84f65-t1/5c5fd745-e6fb-4ec7-a9fe-82b1c509e7fb and 29241b2b-1973-480d-af87-85f59cb4c6a1-t0/35d063d2-3386-4417-ae2d-0fcfddefa9ad), so the absence of a namespace-scoped grant of patch on configmaps is unverified; only the cluster-scoped ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding were observed.

traces_search_by_tags with service=rate, geo, search and reservation and tags error=true each returned no matching trace (status no_data: fb09fca8-6993-45ff-b9e6-bec0f3906324-t0/21b98b69-dc75-4f1d-b644-86a00fa884ea, -t1/a9cde646-107e-49d4-9b3c-bdbe521b980f, -t2/54104046-e0c9-4a34-87ab-4a9bea3838c4, -t3/d92bb1ae-0a21-4ef3-ab34-47c9cded1018); an empty result shows only that those queries matched nothing in the sampled view, so absence of error spans for those services is unknown rather than proven.

It is unknown what consumes ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token (label source: reservation-maintenance) and whether its stuck Terminating state blocks any reservation workflow; no component was observed reading it and its cleanup-token value is redacted and cannot be read.

It is unknown whether the failure-admin-rate / failure-admin-geo scripts were ever executed or scheduled to run; no execution evidence (revoke command, authorization failure) was found, and change history is not an available integration in this Run.

The scrape targets rate.hotel-reservation:9091 and search.hotel-reservation:9092 (job hotel-reservation-application) reported up=0 at 13:00:02Z, so rate_* and search_* application metrics have no samples; whether this deployment is expected to expose those endpoints is unknown.

The user service and the reservation creation/placement path produced no spans in the sampled view, and a complete call chain cannot be claimed from a sampled view; their behaviour is unchecked rather than healthy.

The Jaeger trace views used here are marked incomplete/truncated (ccd82c6c-6bf5-4042-a597-616d8e79b3d1-t0/907fa0df-5c25-48fd-94ec-6c009bde2a5d and 360bb3df-c6e1-47e6-8d4c-aed5cab891c5-t0/e2229729-d0a4-48b9-9aa5-0a442a9d0ec4), so only the spans shown in them are relied on, not a complete trace population.
next_steps: Compare ClusterRole configmap-cleanup-controller with what controller.py actually calls and, if the intended design is for it to unblock Terminating reservation-cleanup ConfigMaps, grant the missing patch verb on configmaps (recommendation only; no change was made here).

After any RBAC correction, confirm that ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token loses finalizer cleanup.reservations.io/pending-cleanup and disappears, and that the 403 lines stop in cleanup-controller-785f8c5b5b-p26bd logs.

Have a human confirm whether the failure-admin-rate / failure-admin-geo scripts and the rate:9091 / search:9092 metric endpoints are part of this scenario's intended design, since neither showed executed effects in the sampled window.
Extend observability retention, or capture a longer continuous window, so the pre-12:58Z part of the incident window can be examined and error-span queries can return data.

import json
import os
import ssl
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

NAMESPACE = "hotel-reservation"
FINALIZER = "cleanup.reservations.io/pending-cleanup"
LABEL_SELECTOR = "app.kubernetes.io/component=reservation-cleanup"
TOKEN_FILE = [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
CA_FILE = "/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt"
API_SERVER = (
    f"https://{os.environ['KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST']}:"
    f"{os.environ['KUBERNETES_SERVICE_PORT_HTTPS']}"
)
TLS_CONTEXT = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=CA_FILE)


def api_request(method, path, payload=None):
    data = None if payload is None else json.dumps(payload).encode()
    headers = [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
    if payload is not None:
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/merge-patch+json"
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        f"{API_SERVER}{path}",
        data=data,
        headers=[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL],
        method=method,
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, context=TLS_CONTEXT, timeout=10) as response:
        raw = response.read()
        return json.loads(raw) if raw else {}


def reconcile():
    selector = urllib.parse.quote(LABEL_SELECTOR, safe="")
    response = api_request(
        "GET",
        f"/api/v1/namespaces/{NAMESPACE}/configmaps?labelSelector={selector}",
    )
    for configmap in response.get("items", []):
        metadata = configmap.get("metadata", {})
        finalizers = metadata.get("finalizers", [])
        if not metadata.get("deletionTimestamp") or FINALIZER not in finalizers:
            continue

        name = metadata["name"]
        remaining = [item for item in finalizers if item != FINALIZER]
        print(
            f"ConfigMap {name} is Terminating; attempting controller-owned cleanup",
            flush=True,
        )
        encoded_name = urllib.parse.quote(name, safe="")
        api_request(
            "PATCH",
            f"/api/v1/namespaces/{NAMESPACE}/configmaps/{encoded_name}",
            {"metadata": {"finalizers": remaining}},
        )
        print(f"ConfigMap {name} cleanup completed", flush=True)


print(f"cleanup-controller starting namespace={NAMESPACE}", flush=True)
while True:
    try:
        reconcile()
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
        if error.code == 403:
            print(
                "cleanup-controller reconciliation failed: "
                "Kubernetes API denied cleanup request with HTTP 403 Forbidden",
                flush=True,
            )
        else:
            print(
                f"cleanup-controller reconciliation failed: Kubernetes API returned HTTP {error.code}",
                flush=True,
            )
    except Exception as error:
        print(
            f"cleanup-controller reconciliation failed: {type(error).__name__}",
            flush=True,
        )
    time.sleep(2)

ROOT_USER="root"

ADMIN_USER="admin"

mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

echo "Privileges restored successfully"

#!/bin/bash


ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"

ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

TARGET_DB="geo-db"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"

echo "Waiting for MongoDB to start..."
until mongo --eval "print('waited for connection')" > /dev/null 2>&1; do
  sleep 1
done
echo "MongoDB started"

# Create the admin user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating admin user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

# Create the root user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating root user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ROOT_USER', pwd: '$ROOT_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database to root
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ROOT_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ROOT_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"


echo "Initialization script completed"
